title: Reading the grid: how terminals turn pixels into legible text
stressor: multi-column layout, justified text with hyphenation, mixed heading sizes
notes: Self-contained single page, all CSS inline, no script, no network URLs. Designed for a 960x640 viewport (120x40 at 8x16). A three-column layout (column-count: 3, column-gap 28px, faint column-rule) with a column-spanning h1 and lede, and four in-column h2 subheadings. Body paragraphs use text-align: justify with hyphens: auto under lang="en". Prose at 15px/22px fills all three columns. White background, dark text. Prose is original, authored for the Nyala corpus.

placement_gate.reason: A wrong-column paragraph maps its runs onto another column's cells, so eight same-row cell collisions are expected. This is an active render fault whose root cause is deferred (overview item 5); the mean/max/drifted defaults still apply. The placement-score override still admits this fault as a pass, but the paint-referenced displacement leg no longer hides it: it carries the correctness-target thresholds with no override, so the fault surfaces as a logged expected-fail with its real numbers (see paint_displace_note).

paint_displace_note: Un-defers the layout-04 fault. The paint-referenced displacement gate carries NO paint_displace_gate override, so it uses the correctness target (mean-abs below 0.5 cell, max-abs below 1.0 cell, both axes) and breaches on the current unfixed build, reporting the real numbers as a logged expected-fail rather than a silent pass. Measured baseline at 120x40: 91 measured runs, mean abs h 0.121, max abs h 1.000, mean abs v 0.505, max abs v 1.000; the placement-score leg still records collisions 8. Later phases that fix the wrong-column mapping turn this expected-fail green.
